bibl.title: Recommendations for myeloid-derived suppressor cell nomenclature and characterization standards

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A CELL CLASS THAT MAY NOT BE A CELL TYPE - myeloid-derived suppressor cells, named nine years earlier to capture a function rather than a lineage, and now given minimal phenotypic, molecular and functional reporting criteria because the field had drifted from the original intent
span.quote: In an attempt to codify analysis of the nature and clinical significance of these cells, 9 years ago a group of investigators suggested to utilize the term of ‘myeloid-derived suppressor cells' (MDSC), informed by the myeloid origin, the immune-suppressive function and the systemic expansion of MDSC in a cancer-related context 6 . The initial intent to introduce MDSC nomenclature was not to define a novel population of myeloid cells (at that point being clear that MDSC are not a distinct myeloid lineage), but to provide a term that captured the function, origin and heterogeneity of the cells and offered a framework to guide studies on these remarkable players in tumour-dependent immune dysfunction.

span.label: what a paper must report before calling a cell an MDSC, when no marker combination is unique to the class and the defining function is often unmeasurable
span.quote: These gating criteria cannot discriminate monocytes from M-MDSCs and neutrophils from PMN-MDSC since at present there are no combinations of markers unique to MDSC. Presently, the only method allowing for separation of neutrophils from PMN-MDSC is gradient centrifugation using 1.077 g l −1 density (standard Ficoll gradient used for the isolation of mononuclear cells). PMN-MDSC are enriched in low density (mononuclear cell fraction), whereas neutrophils are high-density cells

span.label: minimal reporting standards for mouse and human MDSC: named subsets (PMN-MDSC, M-MDSC, eMDSC) with gating criteria, required functional demonstration of T-cell suppression, and a molecular/biochemical table
span.quote: The ability to suppress immune cells is an important characteristic of MDSC. Although MDSC were implicated in suppression of different cells of the immune system such as NK and B cells 22 23 24 , inhibition of T cells is the ‘gold' standard for evaluation of MDSC function and inhibition of T-cell activity appears to be sufficient for designation of cells as MDSC, provided that they meet the phenotypic criteria described above.

span.label: method
span.quote: MDSC are the subject of intensive research with >500 papers published in 2015 alone. However, the phenotypic, morphological and functional heterogeneity of these cells generates confusion in investigation and analysis of their roles in inflammatory responses. The purpose of this communication is to suggest characterization standards in the burgeoning field of MDSC research.

span.label: a term coined to organise a research programme, adopted by a field publishing 500 papers a year, and drifting away from what it was coined to mean
span.quote: The marked growth of publications over the last years has led to deviation from the original intent of the MDSC nomenclature. The objective of this review article is not to provide a comprehensive analysis of the MDSC biology, which has been done in many recent publications, but to suggest minimal phenotypic, molecular and functional criteria for reporting and classifying MDSCs. We also propose to integrate the increasing observations, in which expansion of cells with MDSC morphology, phenotype and main biochemical features is not accompanied by immune suppression.

span.label: a consensus statement by fifteen investigators proposing definitions, gating criteria and required assays, with the objections to the category stated in the text
span.term: a consensus statement by fifteen investigators proposing definitions, gating criteria and required assays, with the objections to the category stated in the text
span.quote: One of the most controversial aspects of MDSC biology is why cells with the morphology and phenotype similar to neutrophils and monocytes should require a designation of PMN-MDSC and M-MDSC. The main consideration reflects the potent immune-suppressive activity of MDSCs, the basis to define them as functionally different from monocytes and neutrophils. However, in recent years studies have identified unique biochemical and molecular characteristics of MDSC, which demonstrate that they are pathologically activated.

span.label: **A NAME INTRODUCED DELIBERATELY AS A RESEARCH FRAMEWORK, NOT AS A NATURAL KIND**: `THE INITIAL INTENT TO INTRODUCE MDSC NOMENCLATURE WAS NOT TO DEFINE A NOVEL POPULATION of myeloid cells (AT THAT POINT BEING CLEAR THAT MDSC ARE NOT A DISTINCT MYELOID LINEAGE), but to PROVIDE A TERM THAT CAPTURED THE FUNCTION, ORIGIN AND HETEROGENEITY of the cells and OFFERED A FRAMEWORK TO GUIDE STUDIES.` The corpus has definitions built to classify, to diagnose and to enrol. **This one was built to ORGANISE A LITERATURE, and its authors say so**
span.quote: In an attempt to codify analysis of the nature and clinical significance of these cells, 9 years ago a group of investigators suggested to utilize the term of ‘myeloid-derived suppressor cells' (MDSC), informed by the myeloid origin, the immune-suppressive function and the systemic expansion of MDSC in a cancer-related context 6 . The initial intent to introduce MDSC nomenclature was not to define a novel population of myeloid cells (at that point being clear that MDSC are not a distinct myeloid lineage), but to provide a term that captured the function, origin and heterogeneity of the cells and offered a framework to guide studies on these remarkable players in tumour-dependent immune dysfunction.

span.label: AND THE USAGE HAS DRIFTED FROM THE INTENT, MEASURABLY: `The marked growth of publications over the last years HAS LED TO DEVIATION FROM THE ORIGINAL INTENT OF THE MDSC NOMENCLATURE ... We also propose to integrate the increasing observations, IN WHICH EXPANSION OF CELLS WITH MDSC MORPHOLOGY, PHENOTYPE AND MAIN BIOCHEMICAL FEATURES IS NOT ACCOMPANIED BY IMMUNE SUPPRESSION.` **Cells that look like the class and lack the function the class is named for** - and the response is to widen the term rather than to exclude them
span.quote: The marked growth of publications over the last years has led to deviation from the original intent of the MDSC nomenclature. The objective of this review article is not to provide a comprehensive analysis of the MDSC biology, which has been done in many recent publications, but to suggest minimal phenotypic, molecular and functional criteria for reporting and classifying MDSCs. We also propose to integrate the increasing observations, in which expansion of cells with MDSC morphology, phenotype and main biochemical features is not accompanied by immune suppression.

span.label: AND A SUBOPTIMAL TERM KEPT FOR CONTINUITY - THE THIRD SUCH DECISION IN THIS CORPUS: `despite realization that THE TERM `MDSC` MAY NOT BE OPTIMAL, we feel that it is purposeful and SHOULD BE RETAINED TO ASSURE CONSISTENCY as the field continues to develop.` After EWGSOP keeping `sarcopenia` against a term it concedes is better suited, and buck2011's `pragmatic compromise ... legacy usage`
span.quote: Therefore, despite realization that the term ‘MDSC' may not be optimal, we feel that it is purposeful and should be retained to assure consistency as the field continues to develop.

span.label: **AND THE CLASS CANNOT BE APPLIED BY THE INSTRUMENT THAT IS SUPPOSED TO APPLY IT**: `These gating criteria CANNOT DISCRIMINATE MONOCYTES FROM M-MDSCs AND NEUTROPHILS FROM PMN-MDSC since AT PRESENT THERE ARE NO COMBINATIONS OF MARKERS UNIQUE TO MDSC. Presently, THE ONLY METHOD allowing for separation of neutrophils from PMN-MDSC is GRADIENT CENTRIFUGATION.` The definition is by surface markers and the surface markers do not separate the class - the separation is by DENSITY
span.quote: These gating criteria cannot discriminate monocytes from M-MDSCs and neutrophils from PMN-MDSC since at present there are no combinations of markers unique to MDSC. Presently, the only method allowing for separation of neutrophils from PMN-MDSC is gradient centrifugation using 1.077 g l −1 density (standard Ficoll gradient used for the isolation of mononuclear cells). PMN-MDSC are enriched in low density (mononuclear cell fraction), whereas neutrophils are high-density cells

span.label: AND IN TISSUE IT IS NOT HARD BUT IMPOSSIBLE: `In mice, Gr-1 or Ly6G staining is used to identify tumour-associated MDSC. HOWEVER, THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN NEUTROPHILS OR MONOCYTES AND MDSC IN FROZEN OR PARAFFIN-EMBEDDED TISSUES IS IMPOSSIBLE.` The word is the authors'. Most of the world's archived tumour material cannot be classified by this vocabulary at all
span.quote: In mice, Gr-1 or Ly6G staining is used to identify tumour-associated MDSC. However, the distinction between neutrophils or monocytes and MDSC in frozen or paraffin-embedded tissues is impossible.

span.label: AND THE PRECISE NATURE OF A NAMED SUBSET IS UNKNOWN BECAUSE THE ASSAY IS POPULATION-LEVEL: `Since functional, biochemical and genomic characterization is performed on ENTIRE POPULATION of cells, and SINGLE-CELL FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS IS NOT YET FEASIBLE, THE PRECISE NATURE OF PMN-MDSC REMAINS UNCLEAR.` The class is defined per cell and measured per population
span.quote: Since functional, biochemical and genomic characterization is performed on entire population of cells, and single-cell functional analysis is not yet feasible, the precise nature of PMN-MDSC remains unclear.

span.label: **AND THE OBJECTION TO THE CATEGORY IS STATED BY THE PEOPLE DEFENDING IT**: `ONE OF THE MOST CONTROVERSIAL ASPECTS of MDSC biology is WHY CELLS WITH THE MORPHOLOGY AND PHENOTYPE SIMILAR TO NEUTROPHILS AND MONOCYTES SHOULD REQUIRE A DESIGNATION of PMN-MDSC and M-MDSC. THE MAIN CONSIDERATION REFLECTS THE POTENT IMMUNE-SUPPRESSIVE ACTIVITY of MDSCs, THE BASIS TO DEFINE THEM AS FUNCTIONALLY DIFFERENT.` The counter-argument is written into the paper that answers it
span.quote: One of the most controversial aspects of MDSC biology is why cells with the morphology and phenotype similar to neutrophils and monocytes should require a designation of PMN-MDSC and M-MDSC. The main consideration reflects the potent immune-suppressive activity of MDSCs, the basis to define them as functionally different from monocytes and neutrophils. However, in recent years studies have identified unique biochemical and molecular characteristics of MDSC, which demonstrate that they are pathologically activated.

span.label: AND TWO RENAMINGS, EACH WITH ITS REASON: `Initially we and others used the term `GRANULOCYTIC MDSC` to describe PMN-MDSC, BUT NOW WE BELIEVE THAT THE LATTER TERM BETTER DEFINES this MDSC subset, since PMN-MDSC are PHENOTYPICALLY DISTINCT FROM steady-state neutrophils` - and `since SOME IMMATURITY IS A COMMON TRAIT OF ALL MDSC SUBSETS, we propose to define them more properly as `EARLY-STAGE MDSC` (eMDSC)`. The second is the sharper move: **a modifier dropped because it does not DISCRIMINATE**
span.quote: These cells have been defined as immature MDSC and the mouse equivalent is yet to be identified. However, since some immaturity is a common trait of all MDSC subsets, we propose to define them more properly as ‘early-stage MDSC' (eMDSC).

span.label: AND THE CONFUSION HAS A NAMED PRE-HISTORY: `It became apparent that CD11b+ Gr-1+ cells WERE HETEROGENEOUS, which GENERATED UNCERTAINTY IN DESCRIPTION of these cells among different groups of investigators, AN AMBIGUITY AMPLIFIED BY THE USE OF DIFFERENT ACRONYMS TO DEFINE THESE CELLS.` The term was coined to end an acronym proliferation - buck2011's problem, nine years earlier and one field over
span.quote: It became apparent that CD11b + Gr-1 + cells were heterogeneous, which generated uncertainty in description of these cells among different groups of investigators, an ambiguity amplified by the use of different acronyms to define these cells.

span.label: AND THE ACTIVATION STATE THAT JUSTIFIES THE CATEGORY IS DEFINED BY CONTRAST: `CLASSICAL ACTIVATION of neutrophils and monocytes has evolved to protect the host ... IN CONTRAST, PATHOLOGICAL ACTIVATION is the result of PERSISTENT STIMULATION of the myeloid compartment with RELATIVELY LOW-STRENGTH SIGNALS ... these cells ARE NOT ABLE TO PERFORM EFFECTIVELY THE NORMAL FUNCTIONS of myeloid cells and ACQUIRE POTENT IMMUNE-SUPPRESSIVE POTENTIAL.` A class defined by a history of stimulation rather than by a marker
span.quote: Classical activation of neutrophils and monocytes has evolved to protect the host from bacteria and viruses, as well as to provide support for the remodelling of tissues after injury or after resolved inflammation. This activation state is characterized by robust phagocytosis, respiratory burst activity and release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Myeloid activation is relatively short-lived and terminated on cessation of the stimulus. In contrast, pathological activation is the result of persistent stimulation of the myeloid compartment with relatively low-strength signals coming from tumours or sites of chronic inflammation. Myeloid cells generated under these conditions are poorly phagocytic, produce high levels of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, and predominantly anti-inflammatory cytokines 9 . As a result, these cells are not able to perform effectively the normal functions of myeloid cells and acquire potent immune-suppressive potential.

span.label: THE DEFINING FUNCTION HAS A GOLD STANDARD IN SCARE QUOTES AND NO THRESHOLD: `inhibition of T cells is THE `GOLD` STANDARD for evaluation of MDSC function and inhibition of T-cell activity APPEARS TO BE SUFFICIENT for designation of cells as MDSC, provided that they meet the phenotypic criteria` - while elsewhere `it is CHALLENGING TO ASCERTAIN WHAT LEVEL of production of any given effector molecule IS SUFFICIENT for the MDSC suppressive activity`. A criterion that is sufficient and unquantified at the same time
span.quote: The ability to suppress immune cells is an important characteristic of MDSC. Although MDSC were implicated in suppression of different cells of the immune system such as NK and B cells 22 23 24 , inhibition of T cells is the ‘gold' standard for evaluation of MDSC function and inhibition of T-cell activity appears to be sufficient for designation of cells as MDSC, provided that they meet the phenotypic criteria described above.

span.label: AND THE MECHANISM CANNOT STAND IN FOR THE FUNCTION: `A number of molecules produced by MDSCs have been implicated in suppression ... Although important for a thorough understanding of MDSC suppressive mechanism(s), EVALUATION OF THEIR EXPRESSION CANNOT SUBSTITUTE FOR FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS. In different settings MDSCs UTILIZE DIFFERENT MECHANISMS of suppression and IT IS DIFFICULT TO PREDICT WHICH WILL BE MORE PREVALENT.` No marker, no molecule, and no fixed mechanism - only the assay
span.quote: A number of molecules produced by MDSCs have been implicated in suppression (discussed below) including: arginases, NO, ROS, IDO, TGFβ and PGE 2 , among others. Although important for a thorough understanding of MDSC suppressive mechanism(s), evaluation of their expression cannot substitute for functional assays. In different settings MDSCs utilize different mechanisms of suppression and it is difficult to predict which will be more prevalent. It is also challenging to ascertain what level of production of any given effector molecule is sufficient for the MDSC suppressive activity.

span.label: AND THE CLASS IS CUT FROM A CONTINUUM: `Since MDSC ARE A CONTINUUM OF CELLS IN DIFFERENT STAGES OF DIFFERENTIATION, assignment of biochemical and molecular MDSC markers WILL DEPEND ON PRESENTLY INCOMPLETELY DEFINED PROCESSES that govern differentiation stages of altered myelopoiesis, and SOME MARKERS MIGHT THUS BE SHARED by cells with different phenotypes or with mature activated monocytes or neutrophils.` The boundary is drawn across a gradient whose governing processes are not yet described
span.quote: Since MDSC are a continuum of cells in different stages of differentiation, assignment of biochemical and molecular MDSC markers will depend on presently incompletely defined processes that govern differentiation stages of altered myelopoiesis, and some markers might thus be shared by cells with different phenotypes or with mature activated monocytes or neutrophils.

span.label: and one named subset has no counterpart in the model organism: `These cells have been defined as immature MDSC and THE MOUSE EQUIVALENT IS YET TO BE IDENTIFIED` - a class defined in humans, renamed to eMDSC in the same paragraph, with nothing on the other side of the translational bridge to compare it to
span.quote: These cells have been defined as immature MDSC and the mouse equivalent is yet to be identified. However, since some immaturity is a common trait of all MDSC subsets, we propose to define them more properly as ‘early-stage MDSC' (eMDSC).

span.label: requiring a functional demonstration of T-cell suppression, with the input MDSC number TITRATED and the loss of suppression shown as the cells are titrated down
span.note: eliminates: artefacts due to MDSC viability, and designation of cells as MDSC on phenotype alone · outcome: held
span.quote: The ability to suppress immune cells is an important characteristic of MDSC. Although MDSC were implicated in suppression of different cells of the immune system such as NK and B cells 22 23 24 , inhibition of T cells is the ‘gold' standard for evaluation of MDSC function and inhibition of T-cell activity appears to be sufficient for designation of cells as MDSC, provided that they meet the phenotypic criteria described above.

span.label: controls with the SAME PHENOTYPE and preferably the SAME TISSUE, from healthy donors or naive mice
span.note: eliminates: attributing to MDSC what any cell of that phenotype would do - and the paper names the exception, that neutrophils are rarely in the PBMC fraction of healthy donors · outcome: partial
span.quote: The ability to suppress immune cells is an important characteristic of MDSC. Although MDSC were implicated in suppression of different cells of the immune system such as NK and B cells 22 23 24 , inhibition of T cells is the ‘gold' standard for evaluation of MDSC function and inhibition of T-cell activity appears to be sufficient for designation of cells as MDSC, provided that they meet the phenotypic criteria described above.

span.label: density-gradient centrifugation at 1.077 g/l to separate PMN-MDSC from neutrophils
span.note: eliminates: nothing cleanly - `THE LIMITATIONS OF THIS APPROACH ARE UNAVOIDABLE`; the low-density fraction contains activated neutrophils too · outcome: failed

Presently, the only method allowing for separation of neutrophils from PMN-MDSC is gradient centrifugation using 1.077 g l −1 density (standard Ficoll gradient used for the isolation of mononuclear cells). PMN-MDSC are enriched in low density (mononuclear cell fraction), whereas neutrophils are high-density cells

span.label: PMN-MDSC
span.quote: Initially we and others used the term ‘granulocytic MDSC' to describe PMN-MDSC, but now we believe that the latter term better defines this MDSC subset, since PMN-MDSC are phenotypically distinct from steady-state neutrophils (having less granules, altered buoyancy, reduced CD16 and CD62L, and increased arginase 1, peroxynitrite, CD11b and CD66b)

span.quote: One of the most controversial aspects of MDSC biology is why cells with the morphology and phenotype similar to neutrophils and monocytes should require a designation of PMN-MDSC and M-MDSC. span.quote: Classical activation of neutrophils and monocytes has evolved to protect the host from bacteria and viruses, as well as to provide support for the remodelling of tissues after injury or after resolved inflammation. This activation state is characterized by robust phagocytosis, respiratory burst activity and release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Myeloid activation is relatively short-lived and terminated on cessation of the stimulus. In contrast, pathological activation is the result of persistent stimulation of the myeloid compartment with relatively low-strength signals coming from tumours or sites of chronic inflammation. Myeloid cells generated under these conditions are poorly phagocytic, produce high levels of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, and predominantly anti-inflammatory cytokines 9 . As a result, these cells are not able to perform effectively the normal functions of myeloid cells and acquire potent immune-suppressive potential.

span.label: `PMN-MDSC` - replaces `granulocytic MDSC` because the cells are `PHENOTYPICALLY DISTINCT FROM steady-state neutrophils` in six named ways

span.quote: These gating criteria cannot discriminate monocytes from M-MDSCs and neutrophils from PMN-MDSC since at present there are no combinations of markers unique to MDSC. Presently, the only method allowing for separation of neutrophils from PMN-MDSC is gradient centrifugation using 1.077 g l −1 density (standard Ficoll gradient used for the isolation of mononuclear cells). PMN-MDSC are enriched in low density (mononuclear cell fraction), whereas neutrophils are high-density cells

span.quote: In mice, Gr-1 or Ly6G staining is used to identify tumour-associated MDSC. However, the distinction between neutrophils or monocytes and MDSC in frozen or paraffin-embedded tissues is impossible.

span.quote: Therefore, despite realization that the term ‘MDSC' may not be optimal, we feel that it is purposeful and should be retained to assure consistency as the field continues to develop.

span.quote: These cells have been defined as immature MDSC and the mouse equivalent is yet to be identified. However, since some immaturity is a common trait of all MDSC subsets, we propose to define them more properly as ‘early-stage MDSC' (eMDSC).

span.label: `a term that CAPTURED THE FUNCTION, ORIGIN AND HETEROGENEITY of the cells and OFFERED A FRAMEWORK TO GUIDE STUDIES` - explicitly `NOT TO DEFINE A NOVEL POPULATION` and with it `CLEAR THAT MDSC ARE NOT A DISTINCT MYELOID LINEAGE`
span.quote: In an attempt to codify analysis of the nature and clinical significance of these cells, 9 years ago a group of investigators suggested to utilize the term of ‘myeloid-derived suppressor cells' (MDSC), informed by the myeloid origin, the immune-suppressive function and the systemic expansion of MDSC in a cancer-related context 6 . The initial intent to introduce MDSC nomenclature was not to define a novel population of myeloid cells (at that point being clear that MDSC are not a distinct myeloid lineage), but to provide a term that captured the function, origin and heterogeneity of the cells and offered a framework to guide studies on these remarkable players in tumour-dependent immune dysfunction.

span.label: renamed from `immature MDSC` because `SOME IMMATURITY IS A COMMON TRAIT OF ALL MDSC SUBSETS` - the modifier discriminated nothing
span.quote: These cells have been defined as immature MDSC and the mouse equivalent is yet to be identified. However, since some immaturity is a common trait of all MDSC subsets, we propose to define them more properly as ‘early-stage MDSC' (eMDSC).

span.label: `the phenotypic, morphological and functional heterogeneity of these cells GENERATES CONFUSION in investigation and analysis`
span.term: size of the literature the standards address
span.quote: MDSC are the subject of intensive research with >500 papers published in 2015 alone. However, the phenotypic, morphological and functional heterogeneity of these cells generates confusion in investigation and analysis of their roles in inflammatory responses. The purpose of this communication is to suggest characterization standards in the burgeoning field of MDSC research.

Presently, the only method allowing for separation of neutrophils from PMN-MDSC is gradient centrifugation using 1.077 g l −1 density (standard Ficoll gradient used for the isolation of mononuclear cells). span.label: the evidence base for the rename from `granulocytic MDSC`
span.term: phenotypic differences between PMN-MDSC and steady-state neutrophils
span.quote: Initially we and others used the term ‘granulocytic MDSC' to describe PMN-MDSC, but now we believe that the latter term better defines this MDSC subset, since PMN-MDSC are phenotypically distinct from steady-state neutrophils (having less granules, altered buoyancy, reduced CD16 and CD62L, and increased arginase 1, peroxynitrite, CD11b and CD66b)

span.label: `inhibition of T-cell activity APPEARS TO BE SUFFICIENT for designation of cells as MDSC` - while `it is CHALLENGING TO ASCERTAIN WHAT LEVEL of production of any given effector molecule IS SUFFICIENT`. A criterion declared sufficient and left unquantified in the same paper
span.quote: The ability to suppress immune cells is an important characteristic of MDSC. Although MDSC were implicated in suppression of different cells of the immune system such as NK and B cells 22 23 24 , inhibition of T cells is the ‘gold' standard for evaluation of MDSC function and inhibition of T-cell activity appears to be sufficient for designation of cells as MDSC, provided that they meet the phenotypic criteria described above.

span.label: the property the class is named for, whose measurement is population-level, impossible in fixed tissue, and without a stated sufficient level
span.quote: One of the most controversial aspects of MDSC biology is why cells with the morphology and phenotype similar to neutrophils and monocytes should require a designation of PMN-MDSC and M-MDSC. The main consideration reflects the potent immune-suppressive activity of MDSCs, the basis to define them as functionally different from monocytes and neutrophils. However, in recent years studies have identified unique biochemical and molecular characteristics of MDSC, which demonstrate that they are pathologically activated.
